     ## Proposed direction: autonomous swarms with runtime-owned results — 2026-09-11
    Add: /Users/spotted/projects/pi-agent-wave-new-design/tasks/prd-runtime-owned-results.md
    # PRD: Capture worker results without mandatory report files
    
    Status: issue intake complete; runtime implementation and acceptance pending.
    
    Parent scope: [package PRD](prd-package-delegate-graph.md). Design: [autonomous swarms](design-autonomous-swarms.md). Machine-readable intake: [issue JSON](intake-runtime-owned-results.json).
    
    ## Problem and user story
    
    Worker collection currently couples authored report validation, AgentFS export and ledger auditing. A report-format error can spend a repair turn, while a bookkeeping failure after export can reject work that already changed the workspace. Coding and research need durable authored output and explicit task acceptance without a mandatory report file.
    
    As a Pi user, I want useful worker results retained and assessed directly, so that report formatting cannot discard work or spend another model turn.
    
    ## Scope and compatibility
    
    Add a frozen per-run `resultContract` enum: `legacy-v1 | runtime-v1`. The public tool's create operation accepts `resultContract`; the existing chat run-creation commands accept `--result-contract legacy-v1|runtime-v1`. Omission selects `legacy-v1`. Unknown values fail before run creation or dispatch. `runtime-v1` is initially eligible only for build and research; operational-command runs keep their existing execution-proof contract and reject the new option explicitly. Preserve `/delegate`, `/graph`, and `delegate_graph` entry points.
    
    Persist the selected contract independently of the frozen model policy. Migrate existing records idempotently to `legacy-v1`; do not reinterpret reports, verdicts, cancelled runs or historical failures. A running operation cannot change contract. Store schema versions and result-contract versions are separate: current source already calls `migrateToV5`, so do not assume the older umbrella reference to v4 is the current schema.
    
    Keep existing graph definitions, caller-driven dispatch, model selection, same-model budgets and frozen fallback chains. No new scheduler, session autonomy command, role-chain simplification or default change belongs here. `runtime-v1` grants no launch or tool permission. Session-start autonomy and its mode-change races remain slice 2.
    
    All existing legacy gates stay in force. New-contract collection does not read or repair report files, synthesize worker verdicts, or require a derived ledger. A substantive correction is task work under existing budgets, never a formatting repair. Missing answers alone do not justify discarding useful staged artifacts.
    
    ## Decision ownership
    
    | Owner | Writes authoritative facts | Cannot decide |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | ACPX adapter | Attributed public answer chunks, request/session identity, observed termination and tool/source references | Task acceptance or a fabricated worker verdict |
    | Worker lifecycle/collector | Attempt identity, durable outcome, candidate references, credential and cleanup checks | Acceptance from exit code, file existence or transcript text matching |
    | GraphStore | Transactional attempts, candidates, acceptance decisions and conditional graph advancement | Meaning of worker prose |
    | Calling orchestrator | Explicit decision, rationale, task-specific evidence, candidate/revision binding | Override failed identity/ownership/storage checks or frozen policy |
    | Independent reviewer | Authored findings or approval for the combined deliverable | Approve its own implementation or synthesis |
    | Integration owner | Serialized application journal and verified workspace checkpoint | Reapply uncertain external side effects |
    | Optional document exporter | Reconstructible summaries and diagnostics | Invalidate a candidate, settle an operation or advance a graph |
    
    The orchestrator may author an acceptance decision; that is distinct from attributing a verdict to the worker. Runtime code must never infer semantic approval from `end_turn`, exit zero or a regex over ordinary prose.
    
    ## Durable result contract
    
    Use typed, discriminated records with database constraints. The exact SQL migration belongs to implementation, but these identities and state distinctions are required:
    
    - **Attempt:** immutable run ID, operation ID, attempt key, selected agent/model, ACPX session and request identity, AgentFS session, timestamps and contract. Process state is `running | exited | cancelled | failed | interrupted`; termination includes exit/signal and failure cause when known. Unknown post-crash process state requires reconciliation, not a guessed clean exit. Cleanup has its own recorded state and may remain pending after process settlement.
    - **Answer:** attempt-bound private content reference, digest, byte count, chunk ordering and public-output provenance; completeness is `complete | incomplete`. Retain original authored output independently of any parsed envelope. Do not call an arbitrary public progress chunk the final answer. A verified adapter must delimit the relevant response and record ambiguity as incomplete.
    - **Candidate:** immutable ID and digest, attempt key, kind `coding | research | mixed`, answer/artifact references and validation findings. Coding also records base revision, changed-path inventory, ownership audit and content digests. Research retains findings, accessible retrieved material/provenance where available, and source references. No repository diff is required for research.
    - **Decision:** immutable ID, candidate ID/digest, decision author, rationale, evidence references and disposition `accept | correct | block`. Coding acceptance binds the combined revision and check results; research acceptance binds the synthesis digest and independent source-support review. Replacing an assessment appends a new decision; it does not rewrite original output.
    
    Attempt settlement and task completion are different transitions. Collecting a process outcome does not mark the operation completed or advance its graph node. Expose process outcome, pending acceptance, candidate ID and cleanup status through collection and status so a settled attempt is not presented as an executing worker. Extend `op=record` additively for new-contract decision/candidate references; retain its legacy report behavior. Commit a valid decision and graph transition in one conditional store transaction, checking the operation's active attempt and cancellation state. A stale candidate cannot advance a replacement attempt.
    
    Stream output incrementally to mode-600 files in private mode-700 runtime directories, with bounded parser buffers, maximum event size and explicit total-output limits. Do not retain the full stdout/stderr stream in arrays as `runStreaming` currently does. Configure and document finite defaults during implementation. Reaching a limit records incomplete capture and preserves available data; it cannot become successful truncation. Never ingest thoughts, tool stdout or unrelated request output as authored answers. Research tool output may be retained separately as evidence with its own provenance, not promoted to assistant speech.
    
    SQLite transactions cannot atomically commit external files. Write and flush immutable private content first, publish it by atomic rename, then transactionally register its digest/reference and attempt outcome. A crash before registration leaves a recoverable orphan, not accepted work. Verify referenced content before decisions. Essential persistence failure pauses dependent progress, retains the attempt resources needed for recovery and still attempts safe credential cleanup. No workspace mutation or redispatch follows an uncommitted outcome. On restored storage, reconcile the same attempt before launching a replacement.
    
    ## Candidate retention and integration boundary
    
    Audit and stage owned changes into private retained storage before destroying the AgentFS attempt. Do not export directly into the user workspace during collection. Ownership violations, credential integrity failures and unavailable audits prevent integration; useful retained content remains unaccepted diagnostic material. Keep live credentials out of retained candidates.
    
    Writable coding release requires a minimal integration journal in this slice: one serialized owner, declared paths, recorded base/content digests, a recoverable preimage, and durable `prepared | applying | applied | rolled_back | needs_reconciliation` checkpoints. Check the base and ownership again under the integration lock. Refuse changed bases, symlink escapes and conflicts before application. Restart must identify applied versus unapplied files by recorded digests and resume or roll back; an ambiguous workspace pauses for reconciliation. Never rerun arbitrary check/tool commands solely because their acknowledgement was lost.
    
    This is a dependency correction to the original slice order: retaining candidates is not enough to claim end-to-end coding acceptance. Broader parallel candidate integration and the simpler graph remain slice 3. Until this minimum journal passes real filesystem recovery tests, keep writable `runtime-v1` dispatch unavailable and do not declare slice 1 or a research-only release accepted.
    
    Research preserves the existing graph topology, but new-contract terminal acceptance additionally requires a separately authored independent review supplied through the caller-driven workflow. A synthesis alone cannot complete the run. The review receives actual findings and accessible source material; it must not receive only host-private paths it cannot read. This is an acceptance checkpoint, not a hidden scheduler or automatic additional graph node. Existing build review/test/audit stages remain for this slice.
    
    ## Acceptance criteria
    
    - [ ] **AC1 — Compatibility and opt-in:** Omitted options and migrated runs behave as legacy runs; explicit build/research opt-in freezes the new contract. Invalid and unsupported combinations fail before dispatch. Duplicate migration/collection/decision calls do not duplicate events, launches or advancement. Cancelled runs stay cancelled and frozen model locks remain unchanged.
    - [ ] **AC2 — Authored capture:** Real Pi, Codex and Claude adapter evidence proves session/request/attempt attribution and response boundaries before enabling each adapter. Missing or malformed report files cause zero report-repair calls. Thoughts, tool-only output, stale requests, empty public content and terminal events alone cannot become accepted answers. Large/chunked/truncated output respects limits and records completeness.
    - [ ] **AC3 — Durable settlement:** Exit, cancellation, provider failure and interruption settle independently of acceptance. Useful artifacts and research answers survive duplicate collection, cleanup, restart and derived-export failure. Essential storage failure pauses safely without acceptance, lost candidates or replayed commands. Late output cannot overwrite a current attempt.
    - [ ] **AC4 — Coding acceptance:** Audited candidate changes survive teardown, serialize integration against a recorded base and recover from every application checkpoint without duplicate writes. Changed bases and unowned paths are refused. Acceptance binds the combined revision, applicable checks and independent review; missing explanations with useful changes require inspection, not a projected verdict.
    - [ ] **AC5 — Research acceptance:** Read-only investigations and synthesis complete without files in the repository or code tests. Acceptance requires actual retrieved material, attributed findings, a synthesis and independent review of source support/coverage/uncertainty. Unsupported citations, empty synthesis and unavailable essential evidence cause correction/blocking with retained findings, never a formatting retry.
    - [ ] **AC6 — Release proof and measurement:** Both task types pass the recovery matrix and package gates, compatibility invariants are synchronized in AGENTS and both READMEs, and separate coding/research baseline and new-contract measurements report quality and timing honestly. Required real prerequisites and unrun paid evidence are explicit blockers, not simulated successes.
    
    ## Crash and replay proof matrix
    
    Run every shared row for coding and repository-read-only research. Add mixed-task coverage for investigation feeding implementation.
    
    | Boundary/input | Required observation |
    | --- | --- |
    | No report, malformed report, unusable optional envelope | Original answer/candidate retained; no report repair or report-dependent failure |
    | Exit zero without useful activity; thought/tool output only | No semantic success; tool evidence alone cannot replace research synthesis |
    | Missing answer with useful file changes | Candidate retained for inspection, no automatic acceptance |
    | Failed/cancelled/interrupted process with partial output | Terminal attempt outcome plus unaccepted retained candidate; no graph success |
    | Wrong request/session/attempt, late completion after retry | Quarantined diagnostic; current attempt/decision unchanged |
    | Chunk splits across UTF-8/JSON boundaries and over-limit events | Bounded memory and deterministic capture; incomplete content labelled |
    | Crash after content rename, before SQLite registration | Orphan recoverable; no missing-content decision or duplicate launch |
    | SQLite unavailable, disk full, content missing/digest mismatch | Pause dependent progress; no integration; recovery uses same identity |
    | Crash after store commit, before collection acknowledgement | Idempotent return of existing outcome/candidate |
    | Cleanup or optional export fails after essential commit | Core result survives; cleanup remains explicit; export never triggers a worker turn |
    | Cancellation races decision or workspace integration | Conditional decision rejected if cancelled; in-flight application reaches a journal checkpoint or rolls back |
    | Crash before/during/after each file application | Reconcile by base/preimage/result digests; no duplicate application |
    | Independent review rejects code or unsupported research claim | Bounded substantive correction, preserving earlier candidate and decision |
    | Final acceptance acknowledgement is lost | Same decision and graph transition returned exactly once |
    
    ## Implementation sequence and ownership
    
    One implementing agent owns all writable paths unless the user explicitly delegates work. Existing dirty Part C files must receive fresh restore copies before edits; historical verification is not the new baseline.
    
    1. Establish adapter evidence and a matched legacy baseline. Inspect actual installed ACPX adapter behavior without copying credentials into artifacts. Record enabled agent/version pairs and explicit missing prerequisites. Paid live probes/benchmarks need separate user authorization; this intake does not grant it.
    2. Add focused failing tests, then the versioned store contract and conditional settlement/decision transitions. Touch `types.ts`, `store.ts`, command/tool schemas and their tests; use real temporary SQLite stores. Prove migration and replay before changing worker collection.
    3. Implement bounded attributed capture and private candidate retention in the ACPX worker/lifecycle path, with tests first. Separate mandatory persistence and security checks from optional report/ledger export. Keep legacy branches pinned by their existing tests.
    4. Implement the minimal integration checkpoint and explicit coding/research acceptance paths, including independent research review. Exercise real temporary filesystem candidates, actual AgentFS audits and interrupted integration. No replacement filesystem backend.
    5. Synchronize status/help, both READMEs and version-qualified AGENTS invariants. Run the complete package gates and the shared recovery matrix, then collect separately authorized matched live measurements before release acceptance.
    
    Affected components include `scripts/acpx-worker.ts`, `lib/acpx-events.ts`, `lib/acpx-types.ts`, `scripts/delegate_core.py`, `scripts/agentfs-export.ts`, `lib/agentfs-sandbox.ts`, `lib/acpx-settlement.ts`, `scripts/report-prompt.ts`, `scripts/ledger.ts`, `index.ts`, `commands.ts`, `types.ts`, `store.ts`, package metadata if new shipped helpers are added, and package-owned tests. Preserve the headless/Herdr transport boundary under its existing PRD. Do not alter the per-worker supervisor into a scheduler.
    
    ## Measurement and verification
    
    Use matched coding and research tasks, frozen models/budgets, comparable input sizes and repeated runs. Record monotonic durations for queue, startup, model execution, report repair, capture/persistence, audit, staging/export, ledger, cleanup, integration/checks or synthesis, independent review, and total time to acceptance. Record model turns, formatting-only turns, attempts, recoveries, manual interventions and accepted/rejected outcomes. Report overlap and critical-path wall time separately; summed parallel durations are not elapsed time.
    
    Compare defect detection, false acceptance and review findings as well as latency. Report sample counts, failures and skips, with median/tail timing only when sample size supports it. Provider-reported usage/cost retains its provenance; unknown cost remains unknown, never zero. No numerical speedup target or claim precedes the baseline. Offline timing proves local overhead only, not live task speed or quality.
    
    Run the repository's full Node completion glob, listed Bun package checks, Node installation rehearsal, typecheck, pack/publish dry runs using a temporary npm cache, and `git diff --check`. Never publish, mutate the real Pi installation or run migration apply. Tests for pure parsing may use literal event inputs, but these are not adapter compatibility proof; adapter enabling requires real reachable dependencies and real output evidence.
    
    Known environment limitations from the current Part C record: sandbox loopback binding, AgentFS mounting and host process inspection prevented full acceptance. Recheck prerequisites when implementation begins and preserve failures as evidence. No live ACPX compatibility, source-support quality benchmark or runtime-v1 result proof was performed during intake.
    
    ## Difficulty and routing
    
    XL. This crosses the public command boundary, SQLite state, ACPX result capture, Python lifecycle and filesystem integration. Crash consistency and independent research acceptance are release dependencies, while adapter evidence and sandbox prerequisites remain unresolved. Route implementation to Codex for sustained repository work with real dependency verification; an independent review is required before claiming release acceptance.
    
    Open release inputs: authorize paid adapter probes/benchmarks when ready, and supply a capable test environment if the existing sandbox restrictions persist. Scheduler budgets, lifecycle hosting and specialist-review triggers remain later-slice decisions and do not block this issue's result-contract specification.

      # PRD: Capture worker results without mandatory report files
      
      Status: issue intake complete; runtime implementation and acceptance pending.
      
      Parent scope: [package PRD](prd-package-delegate-graph.md). Design: [autonomous swarms](design-autonomous-swarms.md). Machine-readable intake: [issue JSON](intake-runtime-owned-results.json).
      
      ## Problem and user story
      
      Worker collection currently couples authored report validation, AgentFS export and ledger auditing. A report-format error can spend a repair turn, while a bookkeeping failure after export can reject work that already changed the workspace. Coding and research need durable authored output and explicit task acceptance without a mandatory report file.
      
      As a Pi user, I want useful worker results retained and assessed directly, so that report formatting cannot discard work or spend another model turn.
      
      ## Scope and compatibility
      
      Add a frozen per-run `resultContract` enum: `legacy-v1 | runtime-v1`. The public tool's create operation accepts `resultContract`; the existing chat run-creation commands accept `--result-contract legacy-v1|runtime-v1`. Omission selects `legacy-v1`. Unknown values fail before run creation or dispatch. `runtime-v1` is initially eligible only for build and research; operational-command runs keep their existing execution-proof contract and reject the new option explicitly. Preserve `/delegate`, `/graph`, and `delegate_graph` entry points.
      
      Persist the selected contract independently of the frozen model policy. Migrate existing records idempotently to `legacy-v1`; do not reinterpret reports, verdicts, cancelled runs or historical failures. A running operation cannot change contract. Store schema versions and result-contract versions are separate: current source already calls `migrateToV5`, so do not assume the older umbrella reference to v4 is the current schema.
      
      Keep existing graph definitions, caller-driven dispatch, model selection, same-model budgets and frozen fallback chains. No new scheduler, session autonomy command, role-chain simplification or default change belongs here. `runtime-v1` grants no launch or tool permission. Session-start autonomy and its mode-change races remain slice 2.
      
      All existing legacy gates stay in force. New-contract collection does not read or repair report files, synthesize worker verdicts, or require a derived ledger. A substantive correction is task work under existing budgets, never a formatting repair. Missing answers alone do not justify discarding useful staged artifacts.
      
      ## Decision ownership
      
      | Owner | Writes authoritative facts | Cannot decide |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | ACPX adapter | Attributed public answer chunks, request/session identity, observed termination and tool/source references | Task acceptance or a fabricated worker verdict |
      | Worker lifecycle/collector | Attempt identity, durable outcome, candidate references, credential and cleanup checks | Acceptance from exit code, file existence or transcript text matching |
      | GraphStore | Transactional attempts, candidates, acceptance decisions and conditional graph advancement | Meaning of worker prose |
      | Calling orchestrator | Explicit decision, rationale, task-specific evidence, candidate/revision binding | Override failed identity/ownership/storage checks or frozen policy |
      | Independent reviewer | Authored findings or approval for the combined deliverable | Approve its own implementation or synthesis |
      | Integration owner | Serialized application journal and verified workspace checkpoint | Reapply uncertain external side effects |
      | Optional document exporter | Reconstructible summaries and diagnostics | Invalidate a candidate, settle an operation or advance a graph |
      
      The orchestrator may author an acceptance decision; that is distinct from attributing a verdict to the worker. Runtime code must never infer semantic approval from `end_turn`, exit zero or a regex over ordinary prose.
      
      ## Durable result contract
      
      Use typed, discriminated records with database constraints. The exact SQL migration belongs to implementation, but these identities and state distinctions are required:
      
      - **Attempt:** immutable run ID, operation ID, attempt key, selected agent/model, ACPX session and request identity, AgentFS session, timestamps and contract. Process state is `running | exited | cancelled | failed | interrupted`; termination includes exit/signal and failure cause when known. Unknown post-crash process state requires reconciliation, not a guessed clean exit. Cleanup has its own recorded state and may remain pending after process settlement.
      - **Answer:** attempt-bound private content reference, digest, byte count, chunk ordering and public-output provenance; completeness is `complete | incomplete`. Retain original authored output independently of any parsed envelope. Do not call an arbitrary public progress chunk the final answer. A verified adapter must delimit the relevant response and record ambiguity as incomplete.
      - **Candidate:** immutable ID and digest, attempt key, kind `coding | research | mixed`, answer/artifact references and validation findings. Coding also records base revision, changed-path inventory, ownership audit and content digests. Research retains findings, accessible retrieved material/provenance where available, and source references. No repository diff is required for research.
      - **Decision:** immutable ID, candidate ID/digest, decision author, rationale, evidence references and disposition `accept | correct | block`. Coding acceptance binds the combined revision and check results; research acceptance binds the synthesis digest and independent source-support review. Replacing an assessment appends a new decision; it does not rewrite original output.
      
      Attempt settlement and task completion are different transitions. Collecting a process outcome does not mark the operation completed or advance its graph node. Expose process outcome, pending acceptance, candidate ID and cleanup status through collection and status so a settled attempt is not presented as an executing worker. Extend `op=record` additively for new-contract decision/candidate references; retain its legacy report behavior. Commit a valid decision and graph transition in one conditional store transaction, checking the operation's active attempt and cancellation state. A stale candidate cannot advance a replacement attempt.
      
      Stream output incrementally to mode-600 files in private mode-700 runtime directories, with bounded parser buffers, maximum event size and explicit total-output limits. Do not retain the full stdout/stderr stream in arrays as `runStreaming` currently does. Configure and document finite defaults during implementation. Reaching a limit records incomplete capture and preserves available data; it cannot become successful truncation. Never ingest thoughts, tool stdout or unrelated request output as authored answers. Research tool output may be retained separately as evidence with its own provenance, not promoted to assistant speech.
      
      SQLite transactions cannot atomically commit external files. Write and flush immutable private content first, publish it by atomic rename, then transactionally register its digest/reference and attempt outcome. A crash before registration leaves a recoverable orphan, not accepted work. Verify referenced content before decisions. Essential persistence failure pauses dependent progress, retains the attempt resources needed for recovery and still attempts safe credential cleanup. No workspace mutation or redispatch follows an uncommitted outcome. On restored storage, reconcile the same attempt before launching a replacement.
      
      ## Candidate retention and integration boundary
      
      Audit and stage owned changes into private retained storage before destroying the AgentFS attempt. Do not export directly into the user workspace during collection. Ownership violations, credential integrity failures and unavailable audits prevent integration; useful retained content remains unaccepted diagnostic material. Keep live credentials out of retained candidates.
      
      Writable coding release requires a minimal integration journal in this slice: one serialized owner, declared paths, recorded base/content digests, a recoverable preimage, and durable `prepared | applying | applied | rolled_back | needs_reconciliation` checkpoints. Check the base and ownership again under the integration lock. Refuse changed bases, symlink escapes and conflicts before application. Restart must identify applied versus unapplied files by recorded digests and resume or roll back; an ambiguous workspace pauses for reconciliation. Never rerun arbitrary check/tool commands solely because their acknowledgement was lost.
      
      This is a dependency correction to the original slice order: retaining candidates is not enough to claim end-to-end coding acceptance. Broader parallel candidate integration and the simpler graph remain slice 3. Until this minimum journal passes real filesystem recovery tests, keep writable `runtime-v1` dispatch unavailable and do not declare slice 1 or a research-only release accepted.
      
      Research preserves the existing graph topology, but new-contract terminal acceptance additionally requires a separately authored independent review supplied through the caller-driven workflow. A synthesis alone cannot complete the run. The review receives actual findings and accessible source material; it must not receive only host-private paths it cannot read. This is an acceptance checkpoint, not a hidden scheduler or automatic additional graph node. Existing build review/test/audit stages remain for this slice.
      
      ## Acceptance criteria
      
      - [ ] **AC1 — Compatibility and opt-in:** Omitted options and migrated runs behave as legacy runs; explicit build/research opt-in freezes the new contract. Invalid and unsupported combinations fail before dispatch. Duplicate migration/collection/decision calls do not duplicate events, launches or advancement. Cancelled runs stay cancelled and frozen model locks remain unchanged.
      - [ ] **AC2 — Authored capture:** Real Pi, Codex and Claude adapter evidence proves session/request/attempt attribution and response boundaries before enabling each adapter. Missing or malformed report files cause zero report-repair calls. Thoughts, tool-only output, stale requests, empty public content and terminal events alone cannot become accepted answers. Large/chunked/truncated output respects limits and records completeness.
      - [ ] **AC3 — Durable settlement:** Exit, cancellation, provider failure and interruption settle independently of acceptance. Useful artifacts and research answers survive duplicate collection, cleanup, restart and derived-export failure. Essential storage failure pauses safely without acceptance, lost candidates or replayed commands. Late output cannot overwrite a current attempt.
      - [ ] **AC4 — Coding acceptance:** Audited candidate changes survive teardown, serialize integration against a recorded base and recover from every application checkpoint without duplicate writes. Changed bases and unowned paths are refused. Acceptance binds the combined revision, applicable checks and independent review; missing explanations with useful changes require inspection, not a projected verdict.
      - [ ] **AC5 — Research acceptance:** Read-only investigations and synthesis complete without files in the repository or code tests. Acceptance requires actual retrieved material, attributed findings, a synthesis and independent review of source support/coverage/uncertainty. Unsupported citations, empty synthesis and unavailable essential evidence cause correction/blocking with retained findings, never a formatting retry.
      - [ ] **AC6 — Release proof and measurement:** Both task types pass the recovery matrix and package gates, compatibility invariants are synchronized in AGENTS and both READMEs, and separate coding/research baseline and new-contract measurements report quality and timing honestly. Required real prerequisites and unrun paid evidence are explicit blockers, not simulated successes.
      
      ## Crash and replay proof matrix
      
      Run every shared row for coding and repository-read-only research. Add mixed-task coverage for investigation feeding implementation.
      
      | Boundary/input | Required observation |
      | --- | --- |
      | No report, malformed report, unusable optional envelope | Original answer/candidate retained; no report repair or report-dependent failure |
      | Exit zero without useful activity; thought/tool output only | No semantic success; tool evidence alone cannot replace research synthesis |
      | Missing answer with useful file changes | Candidate retained for inspection, no automatic acceptance |
      | Failed/cancelled/interrupted process with partial output | Terminal attempt outcome plus unaccepted retained candidate; no graph success |
      | Wrong request/session/attempt, late completion after retry | Quarantined diagnostic; current attempt/decision unchanged |
      | Chunk splits across UTF-8/JSON boundaries and over-limit events | Bounded memory and deterministic capture; incomplete content labelled |
      | Crash after content rename, before SQLite registration | Orphan recoverable; no missing-content decision or duplicate launch |
      | SQLite unavailable, disk full, content missing/digest mismatch | Pause dependent progress; no integration; recovery uses same identity |
      | Crash after store commit, before collection acknowledgement | Idempotent return of existing outcome/candidate |
      | Cleanup or optional export fails after essential commit | Core result survives; cleanup remains explicit; export never triggers a worker turn |
      | Cancellation races decision or workspace integration | Conditional decision rejected if cancelled; in-flight application reaches a journal checkpoint or rolls back |
      | Crash before/during/after each file application | Reconcile by base/preimage/result digests; no duplicate application |
      | Independent review rejects code or unsupported research claim | Bounded substantive correction, preserving earlier candidate and decision |
      | Final acceptance acknowledgement is lost | Same decision and graph transition returned exactly once |
      
      ## Implementation sequence and ownership
      
      One implementing agent owns all writable paths unless the user explicitly delegates work. Existing dirty Part C files must receive fresh restore copies before edits; historical verification is not the new baseline.
      
      1. Establish adapter evidence and a matched legacy baseline. Inspect actual installed ACPX adapter behavior without copying credentials into artifacts. Record enabled agent/version pairs and explicit missing prerequisites. Paid live probes/benchmarks need separate user authorization; this intake does not grant it.
      2. Add focused failing tests, then the versioned store contract and conditional settlement/decision transitions. Touch `types.ts`, `store.ts`, command/tool schemas and their tests; use real temporary SQLite stores. Prove migration and replay before changing worker collection.
      3. Implement bounded attributed capture and private candidate retention in the ACPX worker/lifecycle path, with tests first. Separate mandatory persistence and security checks from optional report/ledger export. Keep legacy branches pinned by their existing tests.
      4. Implement the minimal integration checkpoint and explicit coding/research acceptance paths, including independent research review. Exercise real temporary filesystem candidates, actual AgentFS audits and interrupted integration. No replacement filesystem backend.
      5. Synchronize status/help, both READMEs and version-qualified AGENTS invariants. Run the complete package gates and the shared recovery matrix, then collect separately authorized matched live measurements before release acceptance.
      
      Affected components include `scripts/acpx-worker.ts`, `lib/acpx-events.ts`, `lib/acpx-types.ts`, `scripts/delegate_core.py`, `scripts/agentfs-export.ts`, `lib/agentfs-sandbox.ts`, `lib/acpx-settlement.ts`, `scripts/report-prompt.ts`, `scripts/ledger.ts`, `index.ts`, `commands.ts`, `types.ts`, `store.ts`, package metadata if new shipped helpers are added, and package-owned tests. Preserve the headless/Herdr transport boundary under its existing PRD. Do not alter the per-worker supervisor into a scheduler.
      
      ## Measurement and verification
      
      Use matched coding and research tasks, frozen models/budgets, comparable input sizes and repeated runs. Record monotonic durations for queue, startup, model execution, report repair, capture/persistence, audit, staging/export, ledger, cleanup, integration/checks or synthesis, independent review, and total time to acceptance. Record model turns, formatting-only turns, attempts, recoveries, manual interventions and accepted/rejected outcomes. Report overlap and critical-path wall time separately; summed parallel durations are not elapsed time.
      
      Compare defect detection, false acceptance and review findings as well as latency. Report sample counts, failures and skips, with median/tail timing only when sample size supports it. Provider-reported usage/cost retains its provenance; unknown cost remains unknown, never zero. No numerical speedup target or claim precedes the baseline. Offline timing proves local overhead only, not live task speed or quality.
      
      Run the repository's full Node completion glob, listed Bun package checks, Node installation rehearsal, typecheck, pack/publish dry runs using a temporary npm cache, and `git diff --check`. Never publish, mutate the real Pi installation or run migration apply. Tests for pure parsing may use literal event inputs, but these are not adapter compatibility proof; adapter enabling requires real reachable dependencies and real output evidence.
      
      Known environment limitations from the current Part C record: sandbox loopback binding, AgentFS mounting and host process inspection prevented full acceptance. Recheck prerequisites when implementation begins and preserve failures as evidence. No live ACPX compatibility, source-support quality benchmark or runtime-v1 result proof was performed during intake.
      
      ## Difficulty and routing
      
      XL. This crosses the public command boundary, SQLite state, ACPX result capture, Python lifecycle and filesystem integration. Crash consistency and independent research acceptance are release dependencies, while adapter evidence and sandbox prerequisites remain unresolved. Route implementation to Codex for sustained repository work with real dependency verification; an independent review is required before claiming release acceptance.
      
      Open release inputs: authorize paid adapter probes/benchmarks when ready, and supply a capable test environment if the existing sandbox restrictions persist. Scheduler budgets, lifecycle hosting and specialist-review triggers remain later-slice decisions and do not block this issue's result-contract specification.

      #!/usr/bin/env -S node --experimental-strip-types
      // Entry point for the real ACPX lifecycle matrix, and the reason it exists rather than a bare
      // `node --test` line: `node --test` exits 0 after skipping every case, so an unconfigured run looks
      // green. This refuses instead. The test file keeps its own skip semantics, because the production
      // audit also drives it with RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX=1 and validates its summary.
      //
      // It dispatches real worker sessions and spends provider credits, so nothing here runs without a
      // configured token file. --dry-run prints the exact command and starts nothing.
      //
      // Environment:
      //   PI_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE  required, must point at an existing raw-token file (Claude case)
      //   RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX        set to "1" here; the test file will not run the cases without it
      //   MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR         where the run writes its per-agent evidence; defaults to
      //                               agent-output/production-acpx-worker-backend/final-matrix at the repo root
      //   ACPX_MATRIX_FILE            rehearsal seam: run a different target file instead of the real
      //                               matrix, so the launch wiring can be proved without provider calls
      
      import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
      import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
      import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
      import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
      
      const supportDir = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
      const packageRoot = resolve(supportDir, "../..");
      const repoRoot = resolve(packageRoot, "../..");
      const defaultEvidenceDir = join(repoRoot, "agent-output/production-acpx-worker-backend/final-matrix");
      
      export function matrixPlan(env, args = process.argv.slice(2)) {
      	const tokenFile = env.PI_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE ?? "";
      	const problems = [];
      	if (!tokenFile) problems.push("PI_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE is not set: the Claude case needs a raw-token file and without it all three cases skip");
      	else if (!existsSync(tokenFile)) problems.push(`PI_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE points at ${tokenFile}, which does not exist`);
      
      	const target = env.ACPX_MATRIX_FILE && env.ACPX_MATRIX_FILE.length > 0 ? env.ACPX_MATRIX_FILE : join(packageRoot, "test/acpx-real-matrix.test.ts");
      	if (!existsSync(target)) problems.push(`matrix target ${target} does not exist`);
      
      	const evidenceDir = env.MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR && env.MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR.length > 0 ? env.MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR : defaultEvidenceDir;
      	return {
      		dryRun: args.includes("--dry-run"),
      		problems,
      		target,
      		evidenceDir,
      		command: {
      			executable: process.execPath,
      			args: ["--experimental-strip-types", "--test", target],
      			cwd: repoRoot,
      			env: { RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX: "1", MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR: evidenceDir },
      		},
      	};
      }
      
      function main() {
      	const plan = matrixPlan(process.env);
      	if (plan.problems.length > 0) {
      		console.log("refusing to start: the real matrix is not configured.");
      		for (const problem of plan.problems) console.log(`  - ${problem}`);
      		console.log("  - RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX is set by this script; the matrix cases skip unless it is 1, which is why a bare runner can report passes that never happened.");
      		console.log("  - MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR defaults to agent-output/production-acpx-worker-backend/final-matrix; set it to keep evidence somewhere else.");
      		console.log("Nothing ran, so nothing is proven. Run with --dry-run to print the command without starting a session.");
      		return 1;
      	}
      	const { executable, args, cwd, env } = plan.command;
      	if (plan.dryRun) {
      		console.log(`would run: ${executable} ${args.join(" ")}`);
      		console.log(`  cwd: ${cwd}`);
      		console.log(`  env: RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX=${env.RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX} MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR=${env.MATRIX_EVIDENCE_DIR}`);
      		console.log("dry run: no ACPX session was started and no provider credit was spent.");
      		return 0;
      	}
      	console.log(`starting real ACPX sessions (pi, codex, claude) with RUN_REAL_ACPX_MATRIX=1; evidence goes to ${plan.evidenceDir}`);

      	// it runs as a worker: it hides its output and exits 0 even when the tests inside it failed. The
      	// variable is absent in a normal shell, so stripping it only matters when this script is itself run
      	// from a test or CI step, which is exactly when a swallowed result would go unnoticed.
      	const childEnv = { ...process.env };
      	delete childEnv.NODE_TEST_CONTEXT;
      	const run = spawnSync(executable, args, { cwd, env: { ...childEnv, ...env }, encoding: "utf8", shell: false, timeout: 900_000 });
      	if (run.error) {
      		console.log(`could not start the runner: ${run.error.message}`);
      		return 1;
      	}
      	if (run.stdout) process.stdout.write(run.stdout);
      	if (run.stderr) process.stderr.write(run.stderr);
      	return run.status ?? 1;
      }
      
      // The exit code has to be assigned, not returned: a gate that always exits 0 cannot tell a refusal
      // or a failed run from a passing one.
      if (process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === resolve(process.argv[1])) process.exitCode = main();

      	private insertOperation(
      		runId: string,
      		node: NodeName,

      				fixIteration,
      				command ? JSON.stringify(command) : null,
      				task,
      				this.iso(),

      			status: row.status,

      	getOperation(operationId: string): OperationRow {
      		const row = this.db.query<OperationRow, [string]>("SELECT * FROM operations WHERE id=?").get(operationId);
      		if (!row) throw new Error(`unknown operation ${operationId}`);
      		return row;
      	}
      
      	operations(runId: string, currentOnly = false): OperationRow[] {
      		if (!currentOnly) {
      			return this.db.query<OperationRow, [string]>("SELECT * FROM operations WHERE run_id=? ORDER BY created_at,id").all(runId);
      		}
      		const state = this.getState(runId);
      		return this.db
      			.query<OperationRow, [string, string, number, number]>(
      				"SELECT * FROM operations WHERE run_id=? AND node=? AND round=? AND fix_iteration=? ORDER BY created_at,id",
      			)
      			.all(runId, state.currentNode, state.round, state.fixIteration);
      	}
      
      	/** Returns the current dispatchable operations, each with its frozen role route, plus the frozen policy. */
      	next(runId: string): { state: RunState; operations: (OperationRow & { route?: PolicyRoute })[]; policy: FrozenPolicy } {
      		const policy = this.policy(runId);
      		const operations = this.operations(runId, true).map((operation) => ({
      			...operation,
      			route: policy.routes.find((route) => route.role === roleForNode(operation.node)),
      		}));
      		return { state: this.getState(runId), operations, policy };
      	}
      
      	registerAgent(input: AgentRegistration): string {
      		const transport = parseWorkerTransportKind(input.transport);
      		if (transport === "herdr" && (!input.herdrAgent?.trim() || !input.tabId?.trim() || !input.herdrPaneId?.trim())) throw new Error("Herdr agent registration requires agent, tab, and pane identity");
      		if (transport === "headless" && (input.herdrAgent !== undefined || input.tabId !== undefined || input.herdrPaneId !== undefined)) throw new Error("headless agent registration cannot contain Herdr identity");
      		const acpxValues = [input.acpAgent, input.acpxRecordId, input.acpxSessionId, input.acpxState, input.acpxAttemptKey, input.agentFsSessionId, input.agentFsDbPath, input.acpxCancelScript];
      		const hasAcpx = acpxValues.some((value) => value !== undefined);
      		if (hasAcpx && acpxValues.some((value) => typeof value !== "string" || !value.trim())) {
      			throw new Error("agent registration requires complete ACPX provenance");
      		}
      		if (hasAcpx) {
      			parseAcpAgent(input.acpAgent);
      			parseAcpxState(input.acpxState);
      		}
      		const id = input.id ?? `agent_${randomUUID()}`;
      		const now = this.iso();
      		this.transaction(() => {
      			this.db
      				.query(`INSERT INTO agents(id,run_id,name,node,role,transport,herdr_agent,tab_id,policy_digest,selected_model,model_attempt,acp_agent,acpx_record_id,acpx_session_id,acpx_state,acpx_attempt_key,agentfs_session_id,agentfs_db_path,herdr_pane_id,acpx_cancel_script,status,current_task,created_at,last_activity_at)
      					VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`)
      				.run(
      					id,
      					input.runId,
      					input.name,
      					input.node,
      					input.role,
      					transport,
      					input.herdrAgent ?? null,
      					input.tabId ?? null,
      					input.policyDigest ?? null,
      					input.selectedModel ?? null,
      					input.modelAttempt ?? 0,
      					input.acpAgent ?? null,
      					input.acpxRecordId ?? null,
      					input.acpxSessionId ?? null,
      					input.acpxState ?? null,
      					input.acpxAttemptKey ?? null,
      					input.agentFsSessionId ?? null,
      					input.agentFsDbPath ?? null,
      					input.herdrPaneId ?? null,
      					input.acpxCancelScript ?? null,
      					"pending",
      					input.currentTask,
      					now,
      					now,
      				);
      			this.event({ runId: input.runId, type: "agent_registered", node: input.node, agentId: id, toAgent: input.name, replyTo: input.name });
      		});
      		return id;
      	}
      
      	private allCurrentComplete(state: RunState): boolean {
      		const row = this.db
      			.query<CountRow, [string, string, number, number]>(
      				"SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM operations WHERE run_id=? AND node=? AND round=? AND fix_iteration=? AND status!='completed'",
      			)
      			.get(state.runId, state.currentNode, state.round, state.fixIteration);
      		return row?.count === 0;
      	}
      
      	private previousSlices(runId: string, round: number): SliceSpec[] {
      		const maxFix = this.db
      			.query<{ fix: number | null }, [string, number]>("SELECT MAX(fix_iteration) AS fix FROM operations WHERE run_id=? AND node='implement' AND round=?")
      			.get(runId, round)?.fix;
      		if (maxFix === null || maxFix === undefined) throw new Error("no implementation slices available for retry");
      		return this.db
      			.query<SliceRow, [string, number, number]>(
      				"SELECT slice_id,task,owned_paths_json FROM operations WHERE run_id=? AND node='implement' AND round=? AND fix_iteration=? ORDER BY slice_id",
      			)
      			.all(runId, round, maxFix)
      			.map((row, index) => ({
      				id: row.slice_id ?? `slice-${index + 1}`,
      				name: row.slice_id ?? `slice-${index + 1}`,
      				task: row.task,
      				ownedPaths: JSON.parse(row.owned_paths_json) as string[],
      			}));
      	}
      
      	private createNextOperations(
      		state: RunState,
      		nextNode: NodeName,
      		payload: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
      		round: number,
      		fixIteration: number,
      	): void {
      		if (nextNode === "terminal") return;
      		if (nextNode === "implement" || nextNode === "search") {
      			let slices: SliceSpec[];
      			if (state.currentNode === "thinker_plan" || state.currentNode === "thinker_split") {
      				slices = slicesFromPayload(payload);
      				if (nextNode === "implement") assertDisjointOwnership(slices);
      				if (nextNode === "search") slices = slices.map((slice) => ({ ...slice, readOnly: true, ownedPaths: [] }));
      			} else {
      				slices = this.previousSlices(state.runId, state.round);
      			}
      			const feedback = typeof payload?.feedback === "string" ? payload.feedback : undefined;
      			for (const slice of slices) {
      				const task = feedback ? `${slice.task}\n\nRequired feedback:\n${feedback}` : slice.task;
      				this.insertOperation(state.runId, nextNode, task, round, fixIteration, slice.id, slice.ownedPaths);
      			}
      			return;
      		}
      		const taskByNode: Partial<Record<NodeName, string>> = {
      			review: "Review all current implementation outputs against the frozen thinker plan.",
      			test: "Test the implementation against the frozen thinker plan and current reviewer comments.",
      			audit: "Audit the evidence ledger and current accepted revision.",
      			thinker_synthesize: "Synthesize every search report into one evidence-bearing answer.",
      		};
      		this.insertOperation(state.runId, nextNode, taskByNode[nextNode] ?? nextNode, round, fixIteration);
      	}
      
      	private setState(runId: string, currentNode: NodeName, round: number, fixIteration: number, status: RunStatus): void {
      		const now = this.iso();
      		this.db.query("UPDATE state SET current_node=?,round=?,fix_iteration=?,status=?,updated_at=? WHERE run_id=?").run(
      			currentNode,
      			round,
      			fixIteration,
      			status,
      			now,
      			runId,

      		this.db.query("UPDATE runs SET status=?,updated_at=? WHERE id=?").run(status, now, runId);

      	private projectAgent(row: AgentDbRow): AgentRow {
      		const transport = parseWorkerTransportKind(row.transport);
      		const presentationIdentity = transport === "headless"
      			? headlessPresentationIdentity()
      			: row.herdr_agent && row.tab_id && row.herdr_pane_id
      				? herdrPresentationIdentity(row.herdr_agent, row.tab_id, row.herdr_pane_id)
      				: null;
      		return { ...row, transport, presentation_identity: presentationIdentity };
      	}
      
      	agents(runId?: string): AgentRow[] {
      		const rows = runId
      			? this.db.query<AgentDbRow, [string]>("SELECT * FROM agents WHERE run_id=? ORDER BY created_at,id").all(runId)
      			: this.db.query<AgentDbRow, []>("SELECT * FROM agents ORDER BY created_at,id").all();
      		return rows.map((row) => this.projectAgent(row));
      	}
      
      	events(runId: string, limit = 50, agent?: string): EventRow[] {
      		if (agent) {
      			return this.db
      				.query<EventRow, [string, string, string, number]>(
      					"SELECT * FROM events WHERE run_id=? AND (from_agent=? OR to_agent=?) ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?",
      				)
      				.all(runId, agent, agent, limit)
      				.reverse();
      		}
      		return this.db.query<EventRow, [string, number]>("SELECT * FROM events WHERE run_id=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?").all(runId, limit).reverse();
      	}
      
      	/** Applies an explicit recovery choice to the current failed or blocked operation. */
      	resolveExhaustion(runId: string, operationId: string, decision: "retry" | "defer" | "abort" | "escalate", deferredUntil?: string): RunState {
      		return this.transaction(() => {
      			const state = this.getState(runId);
      			if (state.status !== "awaiting_user" && state.status !== "deferred" && state.status !== "blocked") throw new Error("run is not awaiting a recovery decision");
      			const operation = this.getOperation(operationId);
      			if (operation.run_id !== runId) throw new Error("operation does not belong to run");
      			if (operation.node !== state.currentNode || operation.round !== state.round || operation.fix_iteration !== state.fixIteration) {
      				throw new Error("operation is stale for current graph state");
      			}
      			if (state.status === "blocked" && operation.status !== "blocked") throw new Error("recovery requires an explicitly blocked operation");
      			if (operation.status !== "blocked" && operation.status !== "failed") throw new Error("operation is not awaiting recovery");
      			if (decision === "retry") {
      				this.db
      					.query("UPDATE operations SET status='pending',agent_id=NULL,report_path=NULL,verdict=NULL,transient_attempts=0,classifier_reason=NULL,last_error=NULL,retry_reason='operator-approved-retry',fallback_reason=NULL,retry_not_before=NULL,started_at=NULL,finished_at=NULL WHERE id=?")
      					.run(operationId);
      				const unresolved = this.db.query<CountRow, [string, string, number, number]>(
      					"SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM operations WHERE run_id=? AND node=? AND round=? AND fix_iteration=? AND status IN ('failed','blocked')",
      				).get(runId, operation.node, operation.round, operation.fix_iteration);
      				this.setState(runId, operation.node, operation.round, operation.fix_iteration, unresolved?.count ? "awaiting_user" : "active");
      				this.event({ runId, type: "resume", node: operation.node, operationId, agentId: operation.agent_id ?? undefined, toAgent: roleForNode(operation.node), replyTo: roleForNode(operation.node), payload: {
      					previousAttempt: { agentId: operation.agent_id, status: operation.status, reportPath: operation.report_path, verdict: operation.verdict, error: operation.last_error },
      				} });
      			} else if (decision === "defer") {
      				if (!deferredUntil) throw new Error("deferredUntil is required");
      				this.setState(runId, operation.node, operation.round, operation.fix_iteration, "deferred");
      				this.event({ runId, type: "deferral", node: operation.node, operationId, toAgent: roleForNode(operation.node), replyTo: roleForNode(operation.node), payload: { deferredUntil } });
      			} else {
      				const status: RunStatus = decision === "abort" ? "cancelled" : "blocked";
      				const operationStatus: OperationStatus = decision === "abort" ? "cancelled" : "blocked";
      				this.db.query("UPDATE operations SET status=?,finished_at=? WHERE id=?").run(operationStatus, this.iso(), operationId);
      				this.setState(runId, operation.node, operation.round, operation.fix_iteration, status);
      				this.event({ runId, type: decision, node: operation.node, operationId, toAgent: "user", replyTo: "user" });
      			}
      			return this.getState(runId);
      		});
      	}
      
      	/** Retains a private post-mortem bundle beside the graph database for a run whose worker never registered. */
      	retainRunDiagnostic(runId: string, name: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): string {
      		const path = join(dirname(this.dbPath), "failures", runId, name);
      		ensurePrivatePath(path);
      		writeFileSync(path, `${JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
      		chmodSync(path, 0o600);
      		return path;
      	}
      
      	prune(days: number): number {
      		if (!Number.isFinite(days) || days < 0) throw new Error("days must be non-negative");
      		const cutoff = new Date(this.now().getTime() - days * 86_400_000).toISOString();
      		const rows = this.db
      			.query<{ id: string }, [string]>("SELECT id FROM runs WHERE status IN ('terminal','blocked','cancelled') AND updated_at < ?")
      			.all(cutoff);
      		this.transaction(() => {
      			for (const row of rows) this.db.query("DELETE FROM runs WHERE id=?").run(row.id);
      		});
      		return rows.length;
      	}
      
      	close(): void {
      		this.db.close();
      	}
      }

      export const POLICY_PRESETS = ["cheap", "balanced", "strong", "local", "long-context"] as const;
      const POLICY_NAMES = ["auto", ...POLICY_PRESETS] as const;

      const POLICY_PICKER_ALIASES: Record<(typeof POLICY_PICKER_OPTIONS)[number], (typeof POLICY_NAMES)[number]> = {
      	"Auto (recommended)": "auto",
      	Economy: "cheap",
      	Balanced: "balanced",
      	Strong: "strong",
      	"Local only": "local",
      	"Long context": "long-context",
      };
      
      export const POLICY_PICKER_TITLE =
      	"Choose a model policy. Capability floors may promote a role to a stronger tier; the preview shows every promotion. Local only runs a preflight and fails closed before dispatch if any required role cannot meet its capability floor with a local model.";
      
      /** Maps a CLI alias or exact picker label to its tagged union input. */
      export function policyInputFromName(name: string): ModelPolicyInput {
      	const alias = POLICY_PICKER_ALIASES[name as (typeof POLICY_PICKER_OPTIONS)[number]] ?? name;
      	switch (alias) {
      		case "auto":
      			return { kind: "auto" };
      		case "cheap":
      		case "balanced":
      		case "strong":
      		case "local":
      		case "long-context":
      			return { kind: "preset", preset: alias };

      			throw new Error(`unknown policy '${name}'; expected ${POLICY_NAMES.join("|")}`);
      	}
      }
      
      /** Parses an optional leading `--policy <name>` flag, leaving the task text untouched. */
      export function parsePolicyArg(raw: string): { policy: ModelPolicyInput | null; task: string } {
      	const trimmed = raw.trim();
      	if (trimmed !== "--policy" && !trimmed.startsWith("--policy ")) return { policy: null, task: trimmed };
      	const rest = trimmed.slice("--policy".length);
      	const match = /^\s+(\S+)(?:\s+(.*))?$/.exec(rest);
      	if (!match || !match[1]) throw new Error("--policy requires a value: auto|cheap|balanced|strong|local|long-context");
      	return { policy: policyInputFromName(match[1]), task: (match[2] ?? "").trim() };
      }

      /** Parses an optional leading `--policy <name>` flag, leaving the task text untouched. */
      export function parsePolicyArg(raw: string): { policy: ModelPolicyInput | null; task: string } {
      	const trimmed = raw.trim();
      	if (trimmed !== "--policy" && !trimmed.startsWith("--policy ")) return { policy: null, task: trimmed };
      	const rest = trimmed.slice("--policy".length);
      	const match = /^\s+(\S+)(?:\s+(.*))?$/.exec(rest);
      	if (!match || !match[1]) throw new Error("--policy requires a value: auto|cheap|balanced|strong|local|long-context");
      	return { policy: policyInputFromName(match[1]), task: (match[2] ?? "").trim() };
      }
      
      /** Selects the policy input: explicit flag wins, headless defaults auto, TUI picker with cancellation-to-auto. */
      export async function pickPolicy(ctx: ExtensionContext, explicit: ModelPolicyInput | null): Promise<ModelPolicyInput> {
      	if (explicit) return explicit;
      	if (ctx.mode !== "tui") return { kind: "auto" };

    import { afterEach, test } from "node:test";
    import assert from "node:assert/strict";
    import { mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync, chmodSync, symlinkSync } from "node:fs";
    import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
    import { join } from "node:path";
    import { GraphStore } from "../store.ts";
    import { Database } from "../sqlite.ts";
    import { createHeadlessAcpxAttemptIdentity } from "../lib/acpx-types.ts";
    import { assertResultContractAvailable, parseResultContract } from "../lib/runtime-results.ts";
    
    const roots: string[] = [];
    const stores: GraphStore[] = [];
    afterEach(() => {
    	for (const store of stores.splice(0)) store.close();
    	for (const root of roots.splice(0)) rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
    });
    
    function fixture(graph: "build" | "research" = "build") {
    	const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "runtime-results-"));
    	roots.push(root);
    	const store = new GraphStore({ dbPath: join(root, "graph.db") });
    	stores.push(store);
    	const run = store.initRun("runtime", graph, "Investigate or implement", undefined, undefined, "runtime-v1");
    	const operation = store.next(run.runId).operations[0];
    	const identity = createHeadlessAcpxAttemptIdentity({
    		runId: run.runId, operationId: operation.id, role: "thinker", modelAttempt: 0,
    		transientAttempt: 0, selectedModel: "openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol", agent: "codex",
    	});
    	const input = { identity, sessionId: "session-1", requestId: "request-1", policyDigest: store.policy(run.runId).digest };
    	return { root, store, run, operation, input };
    }
    
    test("result contract parsing is strict and public activation stays closed", () => {
    	assert.equal(parseResultContract(undefined), "legacy-v1");
    	assert.equal(parseResultContract("runtime-v1"), "runtime-v1");
    	for (const value of [null, "runtime-v2", "", 1]) assert.throws(() => parseResultContract(value), /result contract/);
    	assert.doesNotThrow(() => assertResultContractAvailable("legacy-v1"));
    	assert.throws(() => assertResultContractAvailable("runtime-v1"), /not enabled.*adapter.*integration.*acceptance/);
    });
    
    test("schema freezes contract independently of policy and preserves legacy runs on reopen", () => {
    	const { store, root } = fixture();
    	const legacy = store.initRun("legacy", "build", "Existing task");
    	const before = store.getRun(legacy.runId);
    	assert.equal(before.result_contract, "legacy-v1");
    	const other = new GraphStore({ dbPath: join(root, "graph.db") });
    	stores.push(other);
    	assert.deepEqual(other.getRun(legacy.runId), before);
    	const db = new Database(store.dbPath);
    	try {
    		assert.throws(() => db.query("UPDATE runs SET result_contract='runtime-v1' WHERE id=?").run(legacy.runId), /immutable/);
    		assert.equal(db.query<{ version: number }>("SELECT MAX(version) AS version FROM schema_version").get()?.version, 6);
    	} finally { db.close(); }
    	assert.throws(() => store.initRun("ops", "operations", "Run a command", undefined, undefined, "runtime-v1"), /operations.*result contract/);
    });
    
    for (const graph of ["build", "research"] as const) {
    	test(`${graph}: duplicate registration and collection retain one candidate without advancing`, () => {
    		const { store, root, run, operation, input } = fixture(graph);
    		const first = store.beginRuntimeAttempt(input);
    		assert.deepEqual(store.beginRuntimeAttempt(input), first);
    		const content = store.retainRuntimeContent(Buffer.from("Authored finding or explanation"));
    		const candidate = graph === "build"
    			? { kind: "coding" as const, answer: content, artifacts: [content], baseRevision: "base-1" }
    			: { kind: "research" as const, answer: content, sources: [content] };
    		const settlement = { attemptKey: input.identity.attemptKey, outcome: { kind: "exited" as const, exitCode: 0 }, candidate };
    		const result = store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement);
    		assert.equal(result.processState, "exited");
    		assert.equal(result.cleanup, "pending");
    		assert.equal(result.acceptance, "pending");
    		assert.equal(result.candidate?.kind, candidate.kind);
    		assert.equal(store.getState(run.runId).currentNode, operation.node);
    		assert.notEqual(store.getOperation(operation.id).status, "completed");
    		const events = store.events(run.runId).length;
    		const reopened = new GraphStore({ dbPath: join(root, "graph.db") }); stores.push(reopened);
    		assert.deepEqual(reopened.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement), result);
    		assert.equal(reopened.events(run.runId).length, events);
    		assert.equal(reopened.next(run.runId).operations[0].runtimeAttempt?.processState, "exited");
    		assert.throws(() => reopened.record({ runId: run.runId, operationId: operation.id, status: "completed", verdict: "READY" }), /runtime-v1.*legacy/);
    		assert.throws(() => reopened.record({ runId: run.runId, operationId: operation.id, status: "running", transport: "headless" }), /runtime-v1.*legacy/);
    		assert.throws(() => reopened.resolveExhaustion(run.runId, operation.id, "retry"), /runtime-v1.*legacy/);
    		assert.throws(() => reopened.settleRuntimeAttempt({ ...settlement, outcome: { kind: "failed", exitCode: 1, error: "conflicting late result" } }), /conflicting.*settlement/);
    	});
    }
    
    test("attempt identity and policy mismatches fail before an operation starts", () => {
    	const { store, run, operation, input } = fixture();
    	assert.throws(() => store.beginRuntimeAttempt({ ...input, policyDigest: "wrong" }), /policy digest/);
    	assert.throws(() => store.beginRuntimeAttempt({ ...input, identity: { ...input.identity, attemptKey: "wrong" } }), /attempt identity/);
    	assert.equal(store.getOperation(operation.id).status, "pending");

    });
    
    test("cancellation retains late process failure but never reopens the graph", () => {
    	const { store, run, input } = fixture("research");
    	store.beginRuntimeAttempt(input);
    	store.cancelRun(run.runId);
    	const settled = store.settleRuntimeAttempt({ attemptKey: input.identity.attemptKey, outcome: { kind: "cancelled", signal: "SIGTERM" } });
    	assert.equal(settled.processState, "cancelled");
    	assert.equal(settled.acceptance, "unavailable");
    	assert.equal(store.getState(run.runId).status, "cancelled");
    	assert.throws(() => store.beginRuntimeAttempt(input), /cancelled/);
    });
    
    test("missing, modified, public or symlink content cannot commit candidate settlement", () => {
    	const { store, input, root } = fixture();
    	store.beginRuntimeAttempt(input);
    	const content = store.retainRuntimeContent(Buffer.from("candidate"));
    	const path = store.runtimeContentPath(content);
    	const settlement = { attemptKey: input.identity.attemptKey, outcome: { kind: "exited" as const, exitCode: 0 }, candidate: { kind: "research" as const, answer: content, sources: [] } };
    	writeFileSync(path, "tampered");
    	assert.throws(() => store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement), /content.*digest/);
    	assert.equal(store.runtimeAttempt(input.identity.attemptKey).processState, "running");
    	writeFileSync(path, "candidate"); chmodSync(path, 0o644);
    	assert.throws(() => store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement), /private/);
    	rmSync(path);
    	const outside = join(root, "outside"); writeFileSync(outside, "candidate", { mode: 0o600 }); symlinkSync(outside, path);
    	assert.throws(() => store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement), /regular|symbolic|symlink/);
    	rmSync(path);
    	assert.throws(() => store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement), /ENOENT/);
    	assert.equal(store.runtimeAttempt(input.identity.attemptKey).processState, "running");
    });
    
    test("essential SQLite failure rolls back outcome and event, preserving retained content for retry", () => {
    	const { store, input } = fixture("research"); store.beginRuntimeAttempt(input);
    	const content = store.retainRuntimeContent(Buffer.from("retained finding"));
    	const settlement = { attemptKey: input.identity.attemptKey, outcome: { kind: "failed" as const, exitCode: 1, error: "provider failure" }, candidate: { kind: "research" as const, answer: content, sources: [] } };
    	const before = store.events(input.identity.runId).length;
    	const db = new Database(store.dbPath);
    	try {
    		db.exec("CREATE TRIGGER fail_result_event BEFORE INSERT ON events WHEN NEW.type='runtime_attempt_settled' BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'essential storage unavailable'); END");
    		assert.throws(() => store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement), /essential storage/);
    		assert.equal(store.runtimeAttempt(input.identity.attemptKey).processState, "running");
    		assert.equal(store.events(input.identity.runId).length, before);
    		db.exec("DROP TRIGGER fail_result_event");
    		assert.equal(store.settleRuntimeAttempt(settlement).processState, "failed");
    	} finally { db.close(); }
    });

      	/** Applies an explicit recovery choice to the current failed or blocked operation. */
      	resolveExhaustion(runId: string, operationId: string, decision: "retry" | "defer" | "abort" | "escalate", deferredUntil?: string): RunState {
      		return this.transaction(() => {
      			const state = this.getState(runId);
      			if (state.status !== "awaiting_user" && state.status !== "deferred" && state.status !== "blocked") throw new Error("run is not awaiting a recovery decision");
      			const operation = this.getOperation(operationId);
      			if (operation.run_id !== runId) throw new Error("operation does not belong to run");
      			if (operation.node !== state.currentNode || operation.round !== state.round || operation.fix_iteration !== state.fixIteration) {
      				throw new Error("operation is stale for current graph state");
      			}
      			if (state.status === "blocked" && operation.status !== "blocked") throw new Error("recovery requires an explicitly blocked operation");
      			if (operation.status !== "blocked" && operation.status !== "failed") throw new Error("operation is not awaiting recovery");
      			if (decision === "retry") {
      				this.db
      					.query("UPDATE operations SET status='pending',agent_id=NULL,report_path=NULL,verdict=NULL,transient_attempts=0,classifier_reason=NULL,last_error=NULL,retry_reason='operator-approved-retry',fallback_reason=NULL,retry_not_before=NULL,started_at=NULL,finished_at=NULL WHERE id=?")
      					.run(operationId);
      				const unresolved = this.db.query<CountRow, [string, string, number, number]>(
      					"SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM operations WHERE run_id=? AND node=? AND round=? AND fix_iteration=? AND status IN ('failed','blocked')",
      				).get(runId, operation.node, operation.round, operation.fix_iteration);

    import { createHash, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
    import { closeSync, constants, fstatSync, fsyncSync, linkSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, openSync, readSync, realpathSync, unlinkSync, writeSync } from "node:fs";
    import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
    import { parseRuntimeContent, type RuntimeContent } from "./runtime-results.ts";
    
    /** Private content-addressed storage; references never contain caller-supplied paths. */
    export class RuntimeContentStore {
    	private readonly root: string;
    
    	constructor(dbPath: string) {
    		this.root = join(realpathSync(dirname(dbPath)), "runtime-content");
    	}
    
    	private directory(): void {
    		mkdirSync(this.root, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    		const stat = lstatSync(this.root);
    		if (!stat.isDirectory() || stat.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error("runtime content directory must be a regular directory");
    		if ((stat.mode & 0o077) !== 0) throw new Error("runtime content directory must be private");
    	}
    
    	path(reference: RuntimeContent): string {
    		const content = parseRuntimeContent(reference);
    		return join(this.root, content.sha256);
    	}
    
    	verify(reference: RuntimeContent): void {
    		this.directory();
    		const path = this.path(reference);
    		const stat = lstatSync(path);
    		if (!stat.isFile() || stat.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error("runtime content must be a regular file, not a symlink");
    		const fd = openSync(path, constants.O_RDONLY | constants.O_NOFOLLOW);
    		try {
    			const opened = fstatSync(fd);
    			if (!opened.isFile() || opened.nlink !== 1) throw new Error("runtime content must be a single regular file");
    			if ((opened.mode & 0o077) !== 0) throw new Error("runtime content must be private");
    			const hash = createHash("sha256");
    			const buffer = Buffer.alloc(64 * 1024);
    			let bytes = 0;
    			for (;;) {
    				const size = readSync(fd, buffer, 0, buffer.length, null);
    				if (size === 0) break;
    				bytes += size;
    				hash.update(buffer.subarray(0, size));
    			}
    			if (bytes !== reference.bytes || hash.digest("hex") !== reference.sha256) throw new Error("runtime content digest mismatch");
    		} finally { closeSync(fd); }
    	}
    
    	retain(bytes: Uint8Array): RuntimeContent {
    		this.directory();
    		const reference = { sha256: createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex"), bytes: bytes.byteLength };
    		const temporary = join(this.root, `.pending-${randomUUID()}`);
    		const fd = openSync(temporary, "wx", 0o600);
    		try {
    			let offset = 0;
    			while (offset < bytes.byteLength) offset += writeSync(fd, bytes, offset, bytes.byteLength - offset);
    			fsyncSync(fd);
    		} catch (error) {
    			closeSync(fd); unlinkSync(temporary); throw error;
    		}
    		closeSync(fd);
    		try {
    			try { linkSync(temporary, this.path(reference)); }
    			catch (error) {
    				if (!(error instanceof Error && "code" in error && error.code === "EEXIST")) throw error;
    			}
    		} finally { unlinkSync(temporary); }
    		const directoryFd = openSync(this.root, constants.O_RDONLY);
    		try { fsyncSync(directoryFd); } finally { closeSync(directoryFd); }
    		this.verify(reference);
    		return reference;
    	}
    }
